newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra pleased with U.S. Pulmicort ruling.
newsitem.headline: Astra pleased with U.S. Pulmicort ruling.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra said on Wednesday it was pleased with the type of approval it had received for its asthma treatment, the Pulmicort Turbuhaler, in the U.S..
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the use of Pulmicort Turbuhaler in the U.S. for adults over the long term and for children aged six plus.
"We got exactly what we had hoped for," Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters.
He said the usage was wider than its competitor Glaxo Welcome had for its asthma drug and so Astra has a bigger target group.

"The competition only has approval to treat children from 12 years old upwards. What we think that means is that the FDA has the view that our product has fewer side effects that Glaxo Welcome's product," he said.
Ternby said Astra had another advantage in that Glaxo Welcome only had its product approved in aerosol form.
Pulmicort Turbuhaler is the first corticosteroid dry powder inhaler for asthma to be approved in the U.S., Astra said.
"We hope that we will get greater interest with our powder inhaler," Ternby said.
He said Glaxo had registered an application in the U.S. seeking approval for an inhaler but Astra's should be out on the market first.
Ternby did not want to comment on the potential or any target sales for the Pulmicort Turbuhaler in the U.S..
"We don't really know how the situation will develop in the U.S.," he said.
Pulmicort Turbuhaler is now approved in 64 countries. Sales in 1996 increased by 17 percent to 4.73 billion crowns ($613.4 million), Astra said.
